newsitem.title: JAPAN: Marubeni sees Japan aluminium demand off in 97/98.
newsitem.headline: Marubeni sees Japan aluminium demand off in 97/98.

text.p: Marubeni Corp expects Japan's imports and domestic demand for primary aluminium to grow slightly more than three percent in the year to March 1997, followed by a dip of 2.3 percent in the next fiscal year.
In a recent report, Marubeni forecast Japan's domestic demand at 2.50 million tonnes in 1996/97, up 3.2 percent, and at 2.44 million tonnes in 1997/98, down 2.3 percent.
The trade house projected Japanese imports at 2.48 million tonnes in 1996/97, up 3.3 percent from the previous year and a 2.3 percent decline to 2.42 million tonnes in 1997/98.
Marubeni forecast that Japan's domestic output of primary aluminium would hold steady at a marginal 18,000 tonnes in both years.

It estimated Western supplies, including net imports from the former Socialist bloc, at 17.6 million tonnes in calendar 1996, up 6.3 percent from the previous year, and at 17.9 million tonnes in 1997, up 1.7 percent.
Marubeni forecast Western world consumption at 17.55 million tonnes in 1996, off 0.3 percent, and 17.9 million tonnes in 1997, up 2.0 percent.
